title: Structure-Guided Semi-Supervised Clustering via Evolving Star Network

problem.claim: Semi-supervised clustering methods face scalability costs from dense similarity graphs or global embedding transformations and incur redundant annotation costs from uniform supervision queries.

gap.claim: Existing approaches do not adequately provide scalable clustering with efficient, structurally informed supervision selection.

contributions.claim: EvoStar is a scalable semi-supervised clustering framework guided by a dynamically evolving star network.
The framework uses a sparse hierarchical star topology, multi-level star initialization, influential-node querying, and local pruning–grafting refinement.
The paper provides a theoretical analysis of EvoStar under tight constraint budgets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly show that EvoStar outperforms baselines under tight constraint budgets.
The authors report robustness to annotation noise.
The authors report O(n log n) time and O(n) space complexity for large-scale deployment.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing methods have high computational and annotation costs.
EvoStar builds and evolves a sparse hierarchical star structure for clustering and supervision.
The evolving topology propagates constraints implicitly while limiting dependence on external inference models.
Experiments report improved quality, noise robustness, and favorable complexity.
A theoretical analysis is provided for tight constraint budgets.

source_observation.claim: Structurally influential nodes are selected for supervision rather than querying uniformly.

interpretation.claim: Active supervision selection may reduce redundant annotation while preserving useful structural information.

application.claim: Interactive clustering systems could prioritize queries using structural influence.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how query influence is defined or when this strategy fails.

source_observation.claim: A sparse evolving topology is used to support implicit constraint propagation with linear space complexity.

interpretation.claim: Sparse adaptive structures may offer a scalability advantage when global graph or embedding operations are costly.

application.claim: Large-scale interactive clustering could use evolving sparse representations to control computational and memory costs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the datasets, workload conditions, or trade-offs behind the reported complexity and quality.
